t: Kathmandu grew from two older settlements, Yambu and Yengal, which tradition says the Licchavi king Gunakamadeva joined into one city, and it prospered on the trade between India and Tibet.
In the Malla period it was one of four fortified cities of the valley, until the Gorkha ruler Prithvi Narayan Shah took it in 1768 and made it the capital of the state that came to be called Nepal.
Rana prime ministers governed from Kathmandu from 1846 to 1950, the monarchy was abolished there in 2008, and the earthquake of 2015 severely damaged its old squares.
dyk: Legend says Kathmandu's valley was once a deep lake, drained when the bodhisattva Manjushri cut the mountain with his sword, and the old city was laid out in the shape of that sword.
ev: A standing figure is dated by its inscription at Maligaon, the oldest known inscription of the valley
The Licchavi dynasty is established in the valley
Arimalla, the first Malla king, begins his rule in the valley
The Malla kingdom divides into three kingdoms, Kathmandu, Bhadgaon and Patan
The Gorkha Kingdom ends the Malla confederation after the Battle of Kathmandu
The Kot massacre begins Rana rule over Nepal
The Constituent Assembly votes in Kathmandu to abolish the monarchy
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake collapses the Dharahara tower and damages Durbar Square

f.founded: The oldest dated find is a statue of 185 CE from Maligaon; tradition holds that the Licchavi king Gunakamadeva joined two older settlements, Yambu and Yengal, into one city, and legend says the valley was a lake drained by Manjushri.
f.where: In the north-western part of the Kathmandu Valley, north of the Bagmati River, at about 1,324 metres above sea level, in central Nepal.
f.known: The Newar towns Yambu and Yengal; the Licchavi city on the trade route between India and Tibet; the Malla kingdom of Kantipur; the Kasthamandap, from which its name comes; the Gorkha conquest of 1768; Rana rule from 1846; the earthquake of 2015
f.today: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal and the seat of Kathmandu District.
